line_numbers_note: Producer file:line references come from the catalog pass at eca9ba0db5 and are approximate (~) where later commits (F1-F7) moved code; classifier names are verified at the generated commit.

areas.title: Ownership
areas.summary: WorkIntent / WorkUnit / WorkUnitLock agreement: who owns a piece of work and which locks it holds.

areas.title: Runs and the queue
areas.summary: Every queued Run has a live SolidQueue claim and every running Run a live worker.

areas.title: Steps and Workflows
areas.summary: Step, Run and Workflow states agree: loops advance, terminal Workflows have no live descendants.

areas.title: Job state
areas.summary: A Job's state matches the work actually running on it, including closed Jobs and intake.

areas.title: Review barrier
areas.summary: Required reviews are evidence about one exact HEAD; nothing downstream runs on stale evidence.

areas.title: Retries and recovery
areas.summary: Retry, resume, auto-retry, circuits and failure classification are bounded and never fight each other.

areas.title: Landing
areas.summary: The repository landing slot, auto-merge and the landing queue.

areas.title: Merge trains
areas.summary: Merge trains are owned while active and only mark members merged with evidence.

areas.title: Epics
areas.summary: Epic serialization, Epic-wide workflows and cross-Job / cross-Epic dependencies.

areas.title: Start blocks
areas.summary: Admission, capability placement, provider availability, rate limits and resource gates always clear or recheck.

areas.title: Workspaces
areas.summary: Workflow workspaces: loss, reconstruction, pruning and cleanup.

areas.title: Concurrency
areas.summary: Cross-cutting races: lost updates, lock acquisition, check-then-act, lock order, executor fencing.

areas.title: Infrastructure Jobs
areas.summary: Main grader, deploy and main-branch repair Jobs as the reconciler covers them.

areas.title: Reconciler agreement
areas.summary: The reconciler only flags states it can repair, never undoes deliberate domain states, and converges.

items.title: A waiting WorkIntent whose gates now pass still has an active WorkUnit
items.producer: WorkIntents::JobWakeup parks a dependent intent while the Launcher's unit exists (deliberate); only a stale wait is abnormal
items.notes: Was 70% of all production repairs: the reconciler and JobWakeup oscillated forever on justified dependency waits. Fixed by skipping waits whose gates still fail; Agreement.after_converges proves convergence.

items.title: A waiting WorkIntent's gates pass but nothing rechecks it
items.producer: missed wakeup after a gate input changes (dependency, provider, admission); WorkIntents::JobWakeup callers not enumerated
items.notes: Sibling of F1 for intents without an active unit; the F1 model (Agreement.after_clears_stale) covers clearing a stale wait, but which events must wake the intent is not modelled.

items.title: A requested WorkIntent that is ready has no WorkUnit working on it
items.producer: unit terminated without TerminalUnitSync moving the intent, or a launch path that requested the intent but never instantiated (WorkUnits::Launcher)
items.notes: Both classifiers return [] unless the Reconciler is invoked with work_intent_id, and no production caller passes one, so this state is never detected in production. Modelled as requestedWithoutActiveUnit in Reconciler.lean.

items.title: An active WorkUnit has no Workflow, so it cannot run but may hold locks
items.producer: WorkUnits::Launcher creates the unit and attaches the workflow in separate steps; a failure between them, or a WorkflowCancellation that nils the workflow
items.notes: The repair (cancelWithoutWorkflow) is proved invariant-preserving; prevention (launch atomically attaches a workflow) is not proved.

items.title: A finished WorkUnit leaves its WorkIntent open (succeeded unit / unsatisfied intent, failed unit / unfailed intent, superseded unit / uncancelled intent)
items.producer: WorkUnit#mark_terminal! / preempt! commit before WorkIntents::TerminalUnitSync runs (after-commit hook lost or raising)
items.notes: Repairs satisfyFromSucceeded / failFromFailed / cancelFromSuperseded are proved to preserve Inv; making the intent sync part of the terminal transition would make the states unreachable.

items.title: When one intent has both a succeeded and a failed unit, success wins regardless of which is newer
items.producer: WorkIntents::TerminalUnitSync outcome selection
items.notes: Low priority: an older success can satisfy an intent whose latest attempt failed.

items.title: A finished WorkUnit still holds locks, blocking all future work on that key
items.producer: legacy rows; mark_terminal!/preempt! release in the same transaction today; update_columns resurrection paths (history #8)
items.notes: Inv proves no terminal unit holds locks under modelled transitions; update_columns writers outside the model are not covered.

items.title: An active WorkUnit attached to a finished Workflow still holds locks
items.producer: Workflow reached terminal without WorkUnits::WorkflowLifecycle / TerminalWorkflowSync marking the unit terminal (after-commit hook lost)
items.notes: Operator-only repair (retire_terminal_work_unit). Unit and Workflow terminal state should move together; not modelled (the Lean model has only workflowTerminal flags).

items.title: A finished parent WorkUnit still has active child WorkUnits
items.producer: parent mark_terminal!/preempt! does not cascade to children (merge-train / bundle child units)
items.notes: Repair cancelChild is modelled; the terminal transition itself does not cascade in the model or the code.

items.title: Each Workflow is owned by exactly one WorkUnit
items.producer: no unique index on work_units.workflow_id; same_runtime_lock_owner? deliberately treats two units on one workflow as one owner (work_unit.rb:304)
items.notes: LockSafety.steps_lock_safe assumes it; Counterexamples.shared shows lock escape without it.

items.title: Finished WorkUnits can become active again (same-attempt retries reuse the unit)
items.producer: AutoRetryBackoff#record!, DeferredPhaseResume#reactivate_terminal_unit_for_active_workflow!
items.notes: Deliberate; the model allows re-entry and proves lock safety anyway.

items.title: AutoRetryBackoff blocks a failed unit and accepts a partial lock set
items.producer: app/services/auto_retry_backoff.rb:12-77 (ensure_locks! returns true if any lock is active)
items.notes: Every resume path re-runs ensure_active_locks!, so the partial set is completed before the unit runs.

items.title: At most one running unit holds any lock key, and a running unit holds every key it needs
items.producer: WorkUnits::Launcher#create_lock!, WorkUnit#ensure_active_locks!, AutoRetryBackoff#ensure_locks!
items.notes: Proved under UniqueRuntime (O1) and the unique-index abstraction; the nil-owner rescue hole (concurrency/lock-acquisition-nil-owner) is outside the model.

items.title: At most one active first-class WorkUnit per (scope, kind), and at most one holding job:<id>
items.producer: idx_work_units_active_dedup_key_unique has a hole when scope_id is nil (work_unit.rb:348-355); materialize_behind_active_lock? kinds acquire the job lock only at start
items.notes: DB-enforced except the nil-scope hole and lockless materialization; see superseded-active-runtime-work for the visible violation.

items.title: A queued Run has no SolidQueue job at all
items.producer: inline-drive successor never enqueued when RunJob exits on SIGTERM / drain / exception (run.rb:397-400, run_job.rb:120-156); crash between Run after_create_commit and perform_later (run.rb:183)
items.notes: The SIGTERM case is documented as 'will be re-enqueued by reaper', so every graceful deploy produces it. Invariant: queued -> has claim or owned by a live inline driver; driver exit must hand the token back.

items.title: A queued Run's SolidQueue job has no execution row, so nothing will ever pick it up
items.producer: true orphans from Syrus's non-transactional deletes (solid_queue_cleanup_job.rb, solid_queue_run_job_pruner.rb:25-28); before F3, also every job waiting on the per-Job concurrency semaphore
items.notes: Was the most frequent applied Run repair (78 in ~9h), mostly misclassified blocked executions; QueueExecution.after_exact proves orphaned iff no execution row. The remaining true-orphan producer (non-atomic pruner deletes) is still open.

items.title: A queued Run sits on a resume/worker queue that no live worker consumes
items.producer: worker or storage that owned the affinity queue died (InstanceVersion.worker_queue_live? false)
items.notes: External fault; model as a worker-death event removing a queue's consumer and prove recovery re-enqueues off the dead queue.

items.title: A queued Run's RunJob crashed before the Run started, leaving the Run queued forever
items.producer: exceptions in RunJob pre-start gates (defer_for_agent_concurrency?, defer_for_actor_share?, defer_for_macos_worker_drain?, run_job.rb:99-151) escape without failing the Run
items.notes: Invariant: a raise from RunJob for run r leaves r failed or a fresh claim exists. No fixture covers it.

items.title: A lost-queue grader_collect Run whose failure is already cached is replayed instead of failed
items.producer: same as dead resume queue / failed execution, for a grader_collect Step with GraderConclusionCache.failed_for_workflow?
items.notes: An optimisation over a lost queue token; not needed for safety. The infrastructure-grader fixture guards that only real failures are cached.

items.title: A Run pinned to one host keeps deferring or re-enqueueing itself and never starts
items.producer: RunJob host-admission deferral and affinity re-enqueue loop for a workflow with worker_storage_key
items.notes: A placement livelock bounded by a 40-deferral budget and a staleness window; a fairness/termination-measure argument, not a safety invariant.

items.title: A queued Run's queue claim never progresses (wedged worker or stale process heartbeat)
items.producer: worker alive but stuck before run.start!, or a claim whose SolidQueue process heartbeat is stale
items.notes: External fault; the stale-claim variant only waits for SolidQueue's own process pruning.

items.title: A running Run has no live worker behind it
items.producer: worker/pod death, OOM; non-agentic claim without a process
items.notes: Not preventable; prove recovery leaves the Run terminal and the Step reopened or failed within the retry budget.

items.title: Queued Runs sit on a paused queue
items.producer: operator paused a SolidQueue queue
items.notes: Operator-intended; the fixture guards that a pause does not orphan an active merge train.

items.title: Worker or storage loss never fails a Job by itself; recovery is bounded and never runs mutable steps off the owning storage
items.producer: RunJob#handle_running_reentry, WorkflowWorkspaceRecovery, RetryFailedStepEnqueuer, distributed grader reroute
items.notes: Fault model: prove a recovery bound and that mutable steps stay pinned to the workspace's storage key.

items.title: A Run is still queued or running although its Step already finished
items.producer: Steps::LifecyclePropagation#cancel_downstream_queued_steps! cancels queued Steps without touching their queued Runs (steps/lifecycle_propagation.rb:58-75); RunJob skip_with_reason! paths
items.notes: Mostly self-heals because RunJob skips such Runs on dequeue. Invariant: step terminal -> all its Runs terminal; every Step terminal event must cancel or skip its own Runs.

items.title: A Step is still queued or running although all its Runs finished
items.producer: RunJob#record_successful_step! commits run.succeed! and step.succeed! separately (run_job.rb:607-619); Workflow#fail! cancel_orphan_active_runs! via update_columns (workflow.rb:482-488); ImmutableReviewHeadBarrier.cancel_run_without_cascade! (immutable_review_head_barrier.rb:113-120); operator/infra retry whose new Run was deferred
items.notes: No grace period: an operator retry of a non-retryable failure whose Run was deferred is re-failed, and reconciling a barrier-cancelled Step cascades the tail (may defeat the barrier's no-cascade intent). Skips (19) are StateSynchronizer refusing queued->succeeded.

items.title: A Step waiting on an in-place git_transport_transient retry is reconciled to failed during its backoff
items.producer: Runs::LifecyclePropagation#scheduled_in_place_step_retry? for IN_PLACE_STEP_CLASSIFICATIONS (runs/lifecycle_propagation.rb:85-133); reconciler exempts only worker_died (pending_worker_died_step_retry?, reconciler.rb ~3596)
items.notes: Probable outright bug: backoff is at least 5 minutes, so the reconciler fails the Step and cascades before AutoRetryJob fires. Step#awaiting_run? already uses the broader 'any pending attempt' rule.

items.title: A review said 'needs work' but no repair iteration was created
items.producer: Step#advance_next_step! after_update_commit lost; StepDispatcher#handle_successful_review_loop_iteration deferring on phase admission or lock conflict (step_dispatcher.rb ~1478)
items.notes: All 14 production firings were skipped ('review loop repair remained deferred'): the classifier cannot tell an intended deferral from a lost one, the same agreement shape as F4.

items.title: A queued Step whose predecessor finished never got a Run
items.producer: Step#advance_next_step! after_update_commit lost; StepDispatcher#create_run_and_enqueue nil returns without a recheck: run_provider_candidate.nil? and !ImmutableReviewHeadBarrier.satisfied_for? (step_dispatcher.rb ~633-656); enqueue_next_runnable_steps! manual/landing pause (~1293)
items.notes: 534 skipped vs 4 applied in ~9h (522 on one Workflow): the classifier fires on legitimately deferred phases and DeferredPhaseResume declines, a classifier/executor disagreement loop.

items.title: A retry-until barrier was cancelled before it ran, leaving its dependent tail queued forever
items.producer: cancellations under Step.suppress_cancel_cascade on a later-reopened workflow (Workflow#cancel_active_descendants!), loop-exit paths exit_review_loop!/cancel_and_skip_to_next! (step_dispatcher.rb ~1533-1558); exact path not pinned
items.notes: Invariant: queued step with a dependency cancelled-without-runs is itself cancelled; suppressed cascades are the hazard.

items.title: A finished Workflow still has queued or running Steps or Runs
items.producer: Workflows::LifecyclePropagation#failed! deliberately keeps the queued tail (lifecycle_propagation.rb:34-41, workflow.rb:341-349); StepDispatcher#hard_fail_workflow!; RunCompletionReconciler#force_state! via update_columns (run_completion_reconciler.rb:395-405); Workflow#cancel! partial failure
items.notes: Mostly produced by design: every Workflow#fail! with a queued tail. Retry already revives cancelled tails (retry_failed_step_enqueuer.rb:529), so fail! could cancel the tail and make 'terminal -> no active descendants' provable. Prod also had 1 failed repair.

items.title: A finished Workflow still has a running OS process or a step that only looks running
items.producer: orphaned SpawnedProcess / heartbeat whose worker died; projection-only running steps (workflow.rb:283-298)
items.notes: Operator-only variant of the same issue kind, reachable only when no persisted Step or Run is active; the external part is SpawnedProcess liveness.

items.title: A Workflow that never started already has a failed Step
items.producer: RunJob fails Steps in pre-start gates while the workflow is still queued (run_job.rb:420-428, 573-582) and the fail_from / hard_fail_workflow! cascade is lost or takes a non-failing branch
items.notes: Invariant: an unsuperseded failed step with no live work implies the Workflow is terminal or a loop continuation is pending.

items.title: A running Workflow has a failed Step but neither fails nor starts the next loop iteration
items.producer: Step#fail_workflow! after_update_commit -> StepDispatcher.fail_from lost or raised; handle_loop_iteration / enqueue_next_loop_iteration! deferring without materializing
items.notes: 5 of the 8 applied repairs were lost loop continuations. fail_from should be part of the Step-fail action.

items.title: A running Workflow has nothing left to run but never finishes
items.producer: lost advance_from / finish_workflow! after the last Step's commit; suppressed-cascade cancels in ImmutableReviewHeadBarrier.invalidate_stale_evidence! (immutable_review_head_barrier.rb:99-105); StepDispatcher#finish_workflow! uses persisted downstream_work_pending? (step_dispatcher.rb ~2424-2460)
items.notes: 8 skipped vs 1 applied: the reconciler's projected 'active' and the dispatcher's persisted 'active' disagree, so the repair is refused every pass. Looks like an outright agreement bug.

items.title: The reconciler and the dispatcher agree on whether a Step is still active
items.producer: persisted steps.state (Workflow#persisted_active_steps, StepDispatcher#downstream_work_pending?) vs Steps::StateProjection#visible_state vs Step#awaiting_run? (step.rb:381-386)
items.notes: Three definitions of 'active Step'. A single predicate should be the proof target; the disagreement drives the skip loops above.

items.title: Each Step attempt has at most one active Run, and each success advances its successors exactly once
items.producer: StepDispatcher#create_run_and_enqueue checks under workflow->step locks; RetryFailedStepEnqueuer#create_run_for! bypasses the funnel (retry_failed_step_enqueuer.rb:282)
items.notes: Low visible gap: the retry path relies on the Step being terminal; an active-Run check under the step lock would make it airtight.

items.title: In a distributed ready set at most one serial (mutable-workspace) Step is active, and serial Steps run in position order
items.producer: StepDispatcher distributed ready set (step_dispatcher.rb ~2209); insertion sites enqueue_next_loop_iteration! and materialize_branch_steps! shift positions with update_all and must use wire_inserted_step_dependencies!
items.notes: Proved by exhaustive check (all Workflows up to 5 Steps, all readiness assignments, all legal cursors): starting what distributed_ready_set picks never starts a Step after an unfinished serial Step, so at most one serial Step runs. The position-filtered cursor is load-bearing (cursor_needed); every advance_from caller passes a just-finished Step, and resume_deferred_phase's direct-create branches target the Step the scan already chose. Not modelled: Step insertion during review re-materialization and grader fan-out, skippable_queued_step?, retry reopening.

items.title: Finished Runs, Steps, Workflows and WorkUnits only reopen through sanctioned paths that restore their invariants
items.producer: update_columns resurrection: DeferredPhaseResume#revive_cancelled_tail_after! (deferred_phase_resume.rb:61), #reactivate_terminal_unit_for_active_workflow! (54, no LockConflict rescue), RunCompletionReconciler#revive_terminal_cleanup_step! / force_success_after_terminal_race!, WorkflowWorkspaceRecovery#requeue!, RetryFailedStepEnqueuer (433-440), repair_executor.rb ~552/907; WorkUnit#mark_running!/block!/unblock! have no terminal guard
items.notes: Theorem: terminal -> non-terminal only via a Reopen event that re-establishes lock and intent invariants. D1 makes unit re-entry intentional, but the other edges are unchecked.

items.title: A Job's state disagrees with what its latest Workflow did
items.producer: silent early returns in Workflows::JobLifecyclePropagation (fail! on newer_active_workflow?, start! for implemented+non_approval_blocking); propagate_start_to_job! skipped when syncing_from_terminal_work_unit; RetryWorkflowEnqueuer#restore_non_failed_retry_state! writes job.state via update_columns (retry_workflow_enqueuer.rb:211)
items.notes: Recurs in production (14 applied). Property: Job.state = f(latest workflow); each silent return in JobLifecyclePropagation is a proof obligation.

items.title: A Job in a non-running state (implemented, failed, triaging, backlog) still has an active Workflow
items.producer: Job transitions made while a workflow is active (Job#unapprove, fail_landing, mark_failed by an older workflow) do not cancel or adopt it; JobLifecyclePropagation#start! silent guards
items.notes: Needs a declared table of legal (job state, active workflow kind) pairs; failed_job_active_repair_work is the legal 'repair in flight on a failed Job' entry of that table (info only).

items.title: A Job is running or landing but no Workflow is working on it
items.producer: workflow terminated without the Job transition (JobLifecyclePropagation silent guards); landing workflow terminal without LandingFailureHandler/MergeTrainFailureHandler reverting the Job
items.notes: Invariant: job in {running, landing} -> an active first-class unit exists. Pair with job-state-matches-latest-workflow; this catches what Plan.for cannot decide.

items.title: A Workflow that is not the Job's current attempt marks the Job failed when it is cancelled
items.producer: Workflows::JobLifecyclePropagation#cancel! (~job_lifecycle_propagation.rb:116) has no active-sibling guard; cancels with start_cancelled_reason / start_blocked_reason / retry_cancelled_reason bypass superseded_cancellation?; newer_active_workflow? only checks newer workflows
items.notes: chat_feedback, rebase and stack_rebase materialize behind an active lock, so a queued second Workflow next to a running one is normal and its cancel can fail the running Job. Likely real bug.

items.title: A Job has two active first-class Workflows at once
items.producer: WorkUnit.active_dedup_key includes the kind (work_unit.rb:348-355), so two first-class kinds on one Job rely on the job lock; materialize_behind_active_lock? kinds take it only at start
items.notes: Invariant: at most one active first-class unit per Job; the dedup key or a job lock must cover every first-class kind.

items.title: A closed Job still has a Workflow working on it
items.producer: before F6: PollPullRequestJob#close_with, PullRequestMergeCloser, GracePeriodExpiryJob, PollExternalPrJob cancelled only job.runs.active before closing; steps closed their own Job mid-run
items.notes: JobClosure.ClosedQuiet proved; closes are deferred to Workflow finish and external closers go through JobClosure.request!. Plain close_with_reason! callers outside Workflows (operator cancel, Epic archive, ingestion, plugin hooks) rely on the step-boundary and RunJob backstops. Prod had 1 failed repair before the fix.

items.title: A closed Job still has an active job-scoped WorkUnit without a Workflow
items.producer: Job#finish_stale_work_units_after_close (job.rb ~1661) is after_update_commit and lost on crash; WorkUnits::Launcher racing the close creates a unit after the callback ran
items.notes: F6 models Workflows on closed Jobs, not bare units; launch must check job.open? under the same lock as the close.

items.title: A closed Job still has a requested or waiting WorkIntent
items.producer: Job#cancel_stale_work_intents_after_close (job.rb ~1674) skips intents with an active unit and only looks at scope_type job; pollers racing the close create intents
items.notes: Member-scoped (Epic / merge-train) intents are never cancelled on close, and an intent skipped because its unit was active is not re-cancelled when the unit later ends.

items.title: A queued Job's latest Workflow was cancelled and nothing replaced it
items.producer: non-deliberate cascade cancels (Steps::LifecyclePropagation#cancelled! -> cancel_workflow_if_idle!, steps/lifecycle_propagation.rb:37-43) and start-time cancels writing start_cancelled_reason
items.notes: Invariant: job queued -> active owner or start-blocked with a recheck; the start-block variant is the allowed waiting state. The fixture guards against retrying when a PR is already published.

items.title: A Job is implemented or approved but has no pull request
items.producer: Job approve guard strict_epic_dependencies_satisfied_for_approval? is literally true (job.rb ~1229) and mark_implemented has no PR guard (job.rb ~755); AutoApprovalRule#approve_after_grader_success! (auto_approval_rule.rb:68-81) fires on grader_collect success before summarize -> pr_open
items.notes: Likely real bug with auto-approval on: the Job goes implemented -> approved with no PR while the initial workflow is still running, and a failing pr_open leaves it there. Cheap, high-value state invariant; no fixture.

items.title: A Job stays in triaging because its classification job vanished
items.producer: lost ClassifyIssueJob queue job
items.notes: Lost-token fault; prove bounded retries via the attempt cap rather than prevention.

items.title: Feedback and repair Workflows on an existing Job never regress its state
items.producer: PollAllPullRequestsJob follow-up workflows, ci_failure / respond / rebase kinds
items.notes: Medium priority; overlaps job-state-matches-latest-workflow for follow-up kinds.

items.title: A Run is queued or running downstream of a required review that no longer approves the current HEAD
items.producer: a repair advances HEAD after the Run was created; ImmutableReviewHeadBarrier#refresh_required_reviews!/invalidate_stale_evidence! (immutable_review_head_barrier.rb:80-107) cancel only review candidates' Runs, not other queued parallel/DAG branches
items.notes: Run creation (under the Workflow lock) and Run start (RunJob) both check the barrier, so a queued Run made stale by a HEAD change is cancelled when it would start. A *running* stale Run needs HEAD to move while it runs; ReadySet.lean shows that cannot happen: only parallel immutable-checkout Steps (graders) run alongside a serial Step, and every HEAD-moving Step is serial. Remaining assumptions: dynamically inserted Steps keep relative order, and retry paths that reopen Steps are not modelled.

items.title: Required-review evidence always refers to the HEAD that is actually pushed
items.producer: ImmutableReviewHeadBarrier::MUTATION_KINDS = implement, respond only; format, generate, apply_suggestions, analyze_and_fix, landing_fix, coding_handoff_fix, agent_rebase, run_skill also move HEAD; reviewed_head_sha falls back to an older step when the latest Run has no head_sha; satisfied_for? is fail-open on a blank sha
items.notes: Proved: when every HEAD move is a tracked implement/respond step, whatever the barrier lets through was approved (tracked_only_push_reviewed). Counterexamples: a format or generate commit after approval is pushed unreviewed while the barrier passes; so is an agent-authored landing_fix or conflict-resolving rebase. The blank-SHA fail-open is harmless unless combined with such an untracked move. No code bug found in the tracked path (implement always records head_sha). Policy question queued as NY1.

items.title: A retry is planned for a failed Run whose Workflow is still running, and every pass refuses it
items.producer: classify_retryable_failures flagged any failed Run controlling its Step; RetryFailedStepEnqueuer / ResumeWorkflowEnqueuer / merge-train rebuild all refuse an active Workflow
items.notes: 168 skipped rebuild_merge_train, 27 retry_failed_step and 4 retry_workflow skips in ~9h; fixed by skipping while the Workflow is queued or running (Agreement.retry_after_actionable).

items.title: A queued auto-retry Workflow is still waiting although its source was superseded by a success
items.producer: Workflow#cancel_superseded_retry_workflows! (workflow.rb:624-653) only cancels kind 'retry' with a lower id, on Jobs with a PR and matching branch; AutoRetryJob materializing a retry after the success is never cancelled
items.notes: The executor comment records a production loop where the requested intent re-materialized retries. AutoRetryJob/launch should check supersession atomically.

items.title: Auto-retry is bounded and its backoff never outlives the attempt
items.producer: AutoRetryAttempt budget, AutoRetryBackoff#record!, runaway protection
items.notes: Termination measure (budget). AutoRetryBackoff#record! re-blocks a failed unit (D2), so the terminal state is not absorbing.

items.title: A worker-died agent Run can be resumed from its provider session, or needs a new attempt
items.producer: worker death during an agentic Run
items.notes: Recovery opportunity after an external fault; only needs the classifier/executor agreement check.

items.title: The same exception keeps failing Runs on the same app revision
items.producer: an application bug or persistent external fault
items.notes: A deliberate circuit breaker; it is the termination guard for automatic retries.

items.title: A Job is under runaway protection and will not retry automatically
items.producer: job.runaway_protection set after too many attempts
items.notes: A deliberate brake, operator-cleared.

items.title: Someone pushed to the PR branch and the Workflow's push was rejected
items.producer: external push to the PR branch
items.notes: External fault; recovery is retry_workflow for the latest attempt, discard_superseded_branch_output otherwise.

items.title: A Run failed on a git error that will not succeed on retry
items.producer: semantic git failure classified non-retryable
items.notes: Operator-only; the fixtures assert it is not reported as a false positive.

items.title: A landing Workflow runs if and only if it holds the repository landing slot
items.producer: before F7: StepDispatcher.capability_worker_deferred? -> WorkflowBlockProjection.record! -> WorkUnit#block!(no_capable_worker) released the landing lock mid-run
items.notes: LandingSlot.SlotExact proved for launch, cannotPlace and finish; parkSurrendering_breaks shows the old behaviour. A true pre-launch capability check is still a follow-up.

items.title: At most one landing per repository at a time, and approved Jobs land in queue order
items.producer: landing:repository:<id> lock writers: Launcher#create_lock!, WorkUnit#ensure_active_locks!, AutoRetryBackoff#ensure_locks!
items.notes: Mutual exclusion is covered by F7's SlotExact; queue order is not modelled.

items.title: A WorkUnit blocked on something only an operator can clear still holds the landing slot
items.producer: legacy rows; AutoRetryBackoff#ensure_locks! (auto_retry_backoff.rb:58-77) re-creates landing:* locks then blocks with a non-external reason
items.notes: no_capable_worker landings now fail and hold instead of blocking (F7); ci_repair_disabled and the AutoRetryBackoff re-lock remain unproved.

items.title: A landing blocked behind an urgent Job before it started still holds the landing slot
items.producer: unit blocked on urgent_job_active after its first Run (no release), whose workflow later returns to queued-before-first-run via retry; no concrete current producer found
items.notes: Generalise: a blocked unit that has not started holds no repository landing lock, for every block reason.

items.title: A Job stays in landing although every unit landing it is blocked externally
items.producer: WorkUnit#block! releases the landing lock but leaves member Jobs in landing; Launcher.start! -> ensure_landing_job_state! lifts the Job before Scheduler.evaluate! (launcher.rb:96-101)
items.notes: F7 removed the no_capable_worker producer for landings; block! still does not defer members for other external reasons.

items.title: A Job being landed by an active landing unit is not in the landing state
items.producer: WorkUnits::Launcher.start! -> ensure_landing_job_state! only lifts job-scoped first-class units (launcher.rb:96-99, 159-169); Workflows::AutoMerge.after_fail lifts after the fact; relaunch via relaunch_context_for_intent!
items.notes: Two definitions of 'active landing work' disagree (the reconciler excludes externally blocked units, RuntimeOwnership.active_landing_work? does not), so a deferred Job can be pushed back into landing: possible defer/re-land ping-pong.

items.title: A landing Workflow is blocked before start (main repair, transient gate)
items.producer: intentional landing start blocks; landing_failure_kind marker left after the gate cleared
items.notes: Liveness: the block is eventually rechecked and the marker is a cache of the gate. Low priority.

items.title: A merge happens only if the Job is approved and its gates pass at the moment of the merge call
items.producer: LandingQueueProcessor#land (landing_queue_processor.rb ~573) locks only the Job row; urgent, Epic sibling and dependency state are read unlocked; Steps::AutoMerge / AutoMergeGate.evaluate pass expected_sha
items.notes: ADR-0005; holds modulo GitHub's expected_sha semantics, which is the real fence.

items.title: A merge train succeeded but a member whose commit landed is marked failed
items.producer: Steps::MergeTrainLand#handle_unverified_member! / reconcile_members_after_landing! rescue (merge_train_land.rb:396-410, 568-571) then finish_landed_train!; inline evidence window starts at workflow.created_at, the repair's at train.created_at
items.notes: Produced by design through two different evidence windows: a member built by an earlier attempt on the same train is rejected inline and accepted by the repair. One shared evidence predicate removes the state.

items.title: A merge train never marks a member merged unless its work is reachable from the landed integration commit
items.producer: Steps::MergeTrainLand member reconciliation; never merge_train_land with a dirty grader barrier
items.notes: The safety half of the evidence property; provable once there is one evidence predicate.

items.title: A merge train is still active but nothing owns it
items.producer: train workflow terminal without MergeTrainFailureHandler.call completing; a preserved train (merge_train_failure_handler.rb:291-360) whose relaunch AutoRetryAttempt was lost past the 10-minute window
items.notes: Classifier counts blocked train workflows as owners but the executor re-check uses only queued/running (minor inconsistency). Needs atomic terminal hooks plus a fairness assumption for preserved relaunches.

items.title: Stack children landed by the same train as their parent are rebased anyway
items.producer: Job#rebase_stack_children_after_successful_parent_close -> StackRebaseCoordinator.parent_merged
items.notes: Fixed with a direct guard; the general property (no Run starts for a closed Job) is F6.

items.title: An Epic-wide Workflow runs alongside other Workflows in the same Epic
items.producer: StepDispatcher.start_workflow -> EpicWorkflowLock.blocking_workflow_for (step_dispatcher.rb:66-84) only checks other Epic-wide workflows, not under an Epic lock
items.notes: An Epic-wide workflow starts while children run and the reconciler cancels the children afterwards (6 applied); two Epic-wide starts can race (check-then-act).

items.title: A Job cancelled to make room for an Epic-wide Workflow is never restarted
items.producer: no finish hook on the Epic-wide workflow re-launches the Jobs it preempted
items.notes: Pair 'cancel(reason = epic lock)' with an obligation discharged when the Epic-wide unit ends; the reconciler is the only relauncher today.

items.title: A Job stays blocked by its Epic although the Epic now releases it
items.producer: Epic#unblock_child_jobs! runs on some Epic/Job events (epic.rb:131, 396, 586; job.rb:1856-1866) but not on every input change of releases_jobs_for_execution?
items.notes: Missed wakeup; better to make blocked_by_epic a derived predicate so it cannot drift.

items.title: Children of a linear Epic never implement in parallel
items.producer: StepDispatcher.epic_sibling_blocking? (step_dispatcher.rb ~347) is a read-only check in start_workflow with no epic:<id> lock for initial work; epic_sibling_turn_winner falls back to queued.first
items.notes: The operator calls this mandatory and epic_dependency_policy is inert. Pure check-then-act over a concurrently mutated set; no concrete double start constructed yet.

items.title: A Job never starts before its Job, Epic and cross-Epic dependencies are satisfied, and starts once they are
items.producer: dependency start blocks recorded with backoff; satisfying a dependency (Job#start_dependent_jobs_after_implementation, job.rb ~939) does not always wake every blocked dependent
items.notes: Safety (no early start) is easy; liveness needs every dependency event to wake its dependents. stale_dependency_start_block is the missed-wakeup symptom.

items.title: A queued Workflow never got its first Run
items.producer: StepDispatcher.start_workflow returns without a Run and without any block record or recheck for provider_routing_held? (step_dispatcher.rb:31-36), the coding-mode hold (58-63) and backlog (43-47)
items.notes: 204 skipped, 0 applied in ~9h: the classifier fires on legitimately blocked workflows and the executor declines ('workflow start remained blocked'); the three recheck-less holds rely on the reconciler alone.

items.title: Every start block or phase deferral either clears or has a scheduled recheck
items.producer: start_workflow urgent_blocking? branch (step_dispatcher.rb ~180-187) records a block with no WorkflowPhaseAdmissionJob; dependency_failed, stack and job_not_ready branches; start_blocked_backoff_active? early return; create_run_and_enqueue nil returns
items.notes: Liveness under fairness of background jobs; proving it pinpoints each branch that relies on the reconciler as its only wakeup.

items.title: A Workflow paused at a phase boundary is not resumed after its admission recheck time
items.producer: lost or delayed WorkflowPhaseAdmissionJob from Launcher.schedule_blocked_recheck! (launcher.rb:140-150)
items.notes: Same kind is also emitted (info) for a queued workflow intentionally waiting on admission; model the recheck job as a token whose loss is a fault.

items.title: A queued Workflow is intentionally waiting for its turn or for main to be healthy
items.producer: Epic-turn serialization; main-health gate
items.notes: Info-only waiting states; only their eventual clearing is a (liveness) obligation.

items.title: Urgent, landing-slot and Epic-turn gates never starve other work forever
items.producer: UrgentWorkGate.progressing 30-minute window; EXTERNALLY_CLEARED_BLOCKED_REASONS allowlist; epic_sibling_turn_winner (step_dispatcher.rb ~374)
items.notes: Fixed three separate times after production starvation; allowlists mean any new externally-cleared reason squats again, in tension with landing-slot-exact.

items.title: Provider unavailability only pauses admission, and recovery re-admits exactly the paused work
items.producer: WorkUnits::StaleProviderRelauncher.stale? (unit blocked on a provider the Job no longer resolves to); open ProviderCircuitBreaker
items.notes: Liveness under fairness; low priority.

items.title: Agent capacity is saturated while Runs are queued
items.producer: running agent Runs at the configured maximum, or a worker data-root alert
items.notes: Observation only; the provable part is the capacity invariant running <= max.

items.title: A Workflow the agent said it cannot proceed with has been blocked for a long time
items.producer: cannot_proceed artifact awaiting the operator
items.notes: Operator wait; exclude from safety proofs.

items.title: A blocked Workflow on a failed Job has a verified checkpoint and could be retried from it
items.producer: BaseRefreshRetryEligibility on a quiescent blocked workflow
items.notes: Recovery opportunity, not a bad state; the negative fixture guards against resuming past a dirty grader barrier.

items.title: A live Workflow's workspace directory is gone
items.producer: disk or node loss
items.notes: Model storage loss as an environment action and prove recovery leaves no Run pinned to the lost storage key.

items.title: A failed Workflow's workspace is about to be pruned
items.producer: retention timer on failed, uncleaned workflows
items.notes: Time-based warning; workspace cleanup only on Workflow terminal (never in a Step ensure) is the related promise.

items.title: Saving Workflow artifacts never reverts a key another process wrote concurrently
items.producer: WorkUnits::WorkflowCancellation#cancel! pre-lock snapshot merge (workflow_cancellation.rb:44-60); Workflow#persist_assigned_external_artifacts wrote every staged key
items.notes: Artifacts.delta_preserves_concurrent proved; deletions of omitted keys are still whole-bag and not modelled.

items.title: Lock acquisition never silently succeeds without a lock row
items.producer: Launcher#create_lock! rescue (launcher.rb ~379-388) and WorkUnit#ensure_active_locks! rescue (work_unit.rb ~293-301) return normally when active_unit_for_lock_key finds no active owner
items.notes: Inconsistent with the dedup path, which raises LockConflict. A lock row left on a non-active unit would make the key permanently lockless for newcomers.

items.title: At most one live worker executes a Run, or any serial Step of a Workflow, at a time
items.producer: RunJob#acquire_run_execution! row lock + time-based lease; handle_running_reentry declares a worker dead after Run::STALE_HEARTBEAT_THRESHOLD (30 min); WorkflowWorkspaceRecovery#requeue! via update_columns
items.notes: No fencing token: a slow-but-alive worker can keep mutating and pushing after being declared dead. Known, accepted (write fence deferred); state as an assumption in the model.

items.title: All code takes row locks in one global order, so lock cycles cannot deadlock
items.producer: RunJob: Run -> Workflow/Step -> WorkUnit -> Job; RetryFailedStepEnqueuer#call: Job -> Step/Run; LandingQueueProcessor#land: Job -> WorkUnit
items.notes: Run->Job vs Job->Run is a potential cycle; today safety comes from with_lifecycle_lock_retry and DB deadlock detection, not ordering.

items.title: Every Workflow is created through WorkUnits::Launcher and every RunJob only by Run#after_create_commit
items.producer: enforced by spec/architecture/workflow_launch_funnel_spec.rb (ADR-0007)
items.notes: Architecture-spec enforced; the Lean statement 'every Workflow has a WorkUnit' needs N:1 allowance (O1).

items.title: An infrastructure or main-branch-repair Job finished its work but stays open
items.producer: workflow-terminal hook skipped or raised; main_branch_repair has no close-on-success hook (mark_implemented closes infra jobs, job.rb ~756)
items.notes: Invariant: infra Job with a terminal latest workflow is closed; F6's apply-on-finish closure path is the natural place to make it atomic.

items.title: The Job repairing a broken main branch is not progressing
items.producer: MainHealthChangedService#stuck_blocking_repair_job
items.notes: A judgement call for the operator, not a structural predicate.

items.title: The reconciler only flags states one of its planned repairs can actually execute
items.producer: WorkEngine::Reconciler classifier predicates vs WorkEngine::RepairExecutor re-checks
items.notes: Agreement.Actionable proved only for retryable_run_failure. The skip counts on the listed kinds (534, 204, 14, 8, 7 in ~9h) are the remaining disagreement loops.

items.title: The reconciler never repairs a state the domain logic deliberately produces, so the two controllers converge
items.producer: WorkEngine::Reconciler vs domain controllers (JobWakeup, StepDispatcher, Workflow#fail! tail)
items.notes: Agreement.Agrees/converges proved for waiting intents; the same check applies to cleanup_blocked_by_active_descendants (fail! keeps the tail on purpose) and active-step-with-terminal-runs (barrier no-cascade cancels).

needs_you.title: Which commits may follow required reviews without a re-review?
needs_you.context: The barrier only tracks implement/respond. In the initial Workflow the grade loop (format, generate) runs after the review loops, so a formatter or generator commit is pushed without any review having seen it. Landing Workflows have no review gates at all, so landing_fix (an agent editing code after approval) and agent conflict resolution during rebases land without review.
options: A. Mechanical commits (format, generate) are trusted; agent-authored commits after review (landing_fix, agent rebases) must be re-reviewed before landing.
B. Everything that moves HEAD after review requires re-review (strictest; formatter changes would trigger review rounds).
C. Today's behavior is intended: reviews cover the implementation, graders cover later fixes. Document it and record it as by design.
needs_you.recommendation: A. Mechanical steps are deterministic and already gated by graders; agent edits after approval are exactly what the barrier exists to catch. Lean then proves 'the last agent-authored commit was reviewed' for every push.
